parsed.explanation: The lemma is false. Make the witness explicit by taking G={E_k:k≥1}, where E_k={x_k,y_1,…,y_{k-1}}. For every n, H_n={x_1,…,x_n,y_n} is a minimal finite transversal of G: deleting x_j misses E_j, while deleting y_n misses E_{n+1}. The H_n are pairwise incomparable. Now F={{c1,c2}}∪{{c2}∪E_k:k≥1} is pairwise intersecting. Its minimal transversals avoiding c2 include {c1}∪H_n, giving infinitely many incomparable minimal finite transversals, which cannot be represented by containment of finitely many B_j. The proof’s induction improperly treats a transversal C as though every other transversal must meet C; that only follows when C itself is a family member. Since all subsequent finiteness and periodicity arguments depend on this lemma, the proof is incomplete.
